purpose: Join of two large tables on their shared key, both sorted by it (Merge Join candidate)
sql:
SELECT o.o_orderkey, count(*) AS lines
FROM orders o
JOIN lineitem l ON l.l_orderkey = o.o_orderkey
WHERE o.o_orderkey < 20000
GROUP BY o.o_orderkey

extra.AI Reason: The query requires grouping by order key after joining orders and lineitems, and a hash aggregate is efficient for this cardinality.
Hash join is chosen to combine the filtered orders with the lineitem table.
Full scan of lineitem is necessary as there is no filter on it.
Build hash table for the filtered orders.
Index scan on orders_pkey is efficient for the range filter on o_orderkey.

differences.text: Aggregate (Sorted) over (orders, lineitem): PostgreSQL uses Sorted aggregation, the AI uses Hashed. Hashed aggregation needs no sorted input but more memory. Sorted aggregation needs sorted input but little memory. The AI's reason: "The query requires grouping by order key after joining orders and lineitems, and a hash aggregate is efficient for this cardinality."

The join of (orders, lineitem): PostgreSQL uses Nested Loop of (orders) with (lineitem). The AI uses Hash Join of (lineitem) with (orders). Hash join suits large inputs. Nested loop suits a small outer input, especially with an index on the inner side. Merge join suits sorted inputs. The AI's reason: "Hash join is chosen to combine the filtered orders with the lineitem table."
Join of (orders, lineitem): outer and inner inputs are swapped. PostgreSQL's outer input is (orders).

Table orders: PostgreSQL uses Index Only Scan on orders using orders_pkey. The AI uses Index Scan on orders using orders_pkey. A sequential scan wins when many rows qualify. An index scan wins when few rows qualify. A bitmap scan sits in between. The AI's reason: "Index scan on orders_pkey is efficient for the range filter on o_orderkey."

Table lineitem: PostgreSQL uses Index Only Scan on lineitem using lineitem_pkey. The AI uses Seq Scan on lineitem. A sequential scan wins when many rows qualify. An index scan wins when few rows qualify. A bitmap scan sits in between. The AI's reason: "Full scan of lineitem is necessary as there is no filter on it."
Only the AI plan has Hash over (orders) (builds the in-memory hash table for a Hash Join). The AI's reason: "Build hash table for the filtered orders."

similarities: Both plans join the tables in the same order (every intermediate join result is the same).
